negotiation.intro: Where the Nov 20, 2026 reruns leave the decision, in plain terms. Draft wording for Matt only; nothing here is sent to any lender.
negotiation.leverage: Go back to Movement and ask whether they can beat these numbers one more time before Monday's decision.
points: Univest Worksheet 1 has the lowest monthly payment: $2,699.94/mo at 7.375%, with $16,237.65 cash to close and $444,806.60 of interest over the life of the loan.

Univest Worksheet 2 is $2,725.49/mo, about $26/mo more than Worksheet 1, but needs only $14,758.94 cash to close, about $1,500 less cash now, at about $10,000 more interest over the life of the loan ($454,004.60, which is $9,198 more than Worksheet 1).

Movement is at $2,738.71/mo and $17,217.70 cash to close, with $463,249.40 lifetime interest and no credits on the sheet. Its replacement assistance program is still unnamed and unpriced, so it counts for nothing in this comparison until it is priced.

5.label: 5% down: Nov 19, 2026 quotes (earlier)
5.note: Earlier quotes, Nov 19, 2026. Both were built on $320/mo taxes (Zillow), not the verified $430.83/mo, so monthly totals run about $111/mo low and cash figures miss roughly $1,443 of added tax escrow. Univest cash figures are the corrected ones: the $500 first-time buyer credit was double-counted on the worksheets (stated $21,505.39 and $20,057.01). Movement's stated cash is $21,932.72; on the real settlement date it computes to about $22,300 (computed, unverified read). Interest over the hold period is computed from rate and loan for this scenario.
